title: Chunky Rectangle Wrap
subtitle: Super-chunky treble stitch rectangle worked in four rows on a 10mm hook
excerpt: A bold rectangle wrap worked entirely in treble crochet using super-chunky yarn on a 10mm hook. The whole piece is four rows deep, making this an accessible first project for anyone learning treble crochet.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Plain treble rectangle construction is a foundational technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A folded rectangle wrap in chunky oatmeal super-chunky yarn. Bold treble stitches clearly visible. Draped over a wooden rail, natural light. Simple and warm styling.

crochet.gaugeText: 7 tr and 4 rows to 10cm over treble stitch using 10mm hook. Swatch before starting.

glossaryTerms.definition: UK treble (tr): yarn over once before inserting the hook, draw up a loop, then work off loops in two steps. UK treble equals US double crochet.
One or more chains worked at the start of a row to bring the hook to the right height for the next row. For treble, ch 3 and count it as the first treble.

content.text: This rectangle wrap measures approximately 165cm wide by 45cm deep and is worked entirely in treble crochet using super-chunky yarn on a 10mm hook. The finished piece is just four rows of stitches, plus the foundation chain. That means the width comes from a long foundation chain and the depth is built quickly in only a handful of rows. Treble crochet is a tall, open stitch that produces fabric with a slight drape. The ch-3 turning chain at the start of each row counts as the first treble, so you skip the first stitch at the base of the chain and work the last treble into the top of the turning chain from the row below.

Yarn: approximately 300g of super-chunky weight yarn (a single skein of most super-chunky yarns is enough). Hook: 10mm. You will also need a tapestry needle and scissors. A tape measure is useful for checking your foundation chain length.
Gauge

7 trebles and 4 rows to 10cm over treble stitch on a 10mm hook. This gauge gives the stated 165cm x 45cm finished size. Super-chunky yarns vary considerably in thickness between brands: check your gauge swatch before working the full foundation chain.
Stitches used
ch: chain
tr: treble crochet (UK)
t-ch: turning chain (ch 3, counts as first tr)
Pattern

At the stated gauge, 165cm requires approximately 117 trebles. The foundation chain is 120 chains (117 stitches plus 3 for the first turning chain). Work a short swatch and count your trebles per 10cm before chaining the full length.
Foundation chain
Ch 120. Lay the chain flat and measure: it should reach approximately 165cm. Adjust the chain count by roughly 7 chains per 10cm if your tension differs.
Row 1
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), tr in 4th ch from hook, tr in each remaining ch to end, turn. (118 sts, including the ch-3 turning chain)
Row 2
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), skip first st (the one at the base of the turning chain), tr in each st across to turning chain, tr in top of turning ch, turn. (118 sts)
Rows 3 and 4
Repeat Row 2 twice more. (118 sts at end of each row)
After Row 4, fasten off and leave a 15cm tail. The wrap now measures approximately 165cm wide by 45cm deep.
Finishing

Weave in all ends with the tapestry needle, working through several stitches on the wrong side. Weave in the tail at the foundation chain in the same way. Trim the ends close to the fabric. The wrap needs no other finishing: the treble stitch produces a neat, stable edge on all four sides.
Care

Follow the care label on your yarn. Super-chunky acrylics are typically machine washable on a cool, gentle cycle. Super-chunky wools require hand washing and drying flat. Do not tumble dry wool or acrylic-blend yarns at high heat.
What to try next

The granny stripe shawl uses the same DK weight rectangle shape but with clustered trebles separated by chain spaces, introducing a stripe colour-change technique. For a longer, more involved rectangle, the basketweave wrap uses aran weight and adds post-stitch texture over the same basic construction. If you enjoyed working with large yarn, try a super-chunky cushion cover as a next step before moving to shaped projects.
